ThingDef.label: pilgrim's token
ThingDef.description: A small token a pilgrim brought home from a holy place far off: a shell, a stone or a scrap of cloth from the place, worn on a cord. It is worth little to anyone but the one who walked for it.

HediffDef.label: fish biting
HediffDef.description: Gave the first fish of the morning back to the water. The fish have been biting well since, and the catch is a little better for the rest of the day.

plain.li: [giveback] The first one goes back to the water, for {GOD}.
[giveback] Back you go, the first catch of the day is {GOD}'s.
[giveback] One back to the water before I keep any, the way I was taught.
[giveback] There, {GOD} has the first, now the rest are mine.
[seen] I saw that splash, the first fish of the day went back to {GOD}.
[seen] Good, the first fish went back, the day will go well now.
[seenother] Did that fish just get thrown back in on purpose?
[seenother] Somebody just tossed a good fish back into the water.
[debtcoin] There's a gold coin on the doorstep, and nobody here dropped it.
[debtcoin] A gold coin, right outside the door, the morning after we paid what we owed.
[debtcoin,doubt] A coin on the step, a trader must have lost it on the way through.

JobDef.reportString: writing up the colony's book of the gods.

plain.li: [look] Here it was, and here I see it with mine own eyes, that the book may say so.
[look] So it is as they told me, and I shall set it down as I find it.
[look] I came to see what {GOD} left here, and I shall write it plain.
[look] Let it be written that the keeper came hither and saw it so.
[lookunnamed] Something was here, as they said, and I know not whose doing it was.
[lookunnamed] I have seen the place, and the book shall say what I saw and no more.
[write] Let it be set down as it was told me, and no word added.
[write] Now to write what was seen this day, while it is yet fresh.
[write] The book wanteth its new pages, and I shall give them.
For {GOD}, and for everything you have.
{GOD} is with us, and {GOD} sees you hiding.
{GOD} wants your walls down, and we are here to do it.
We came in {GOD}'s name, and we go home with your goods.
Call on your own gods, {GOD} is louder.
{GOD} goes before us, so run while you can.
Take them, {GOD} is watching how we fight.
In {GOD}'s name, over the wall with you all.

li.label: given to the god we share
li.description: At the eulogy they were given into the keeping of the god we both hold. It is a little easier to let them go, knowing that.

plain.li: [give] Take {OTHER_objective} into thy keeping, {GOD}, for {OTHER_pronoun} kept faith with thee.
[give] Unto thee, {GOD}, we give {OTHER_nameDef}, and ask that thou keep {OTHER_objective} well.
[give] {GOD}, here is one of thine come home to thee, receive {OTHER_objective} gently.
[give] Into thy hands, {GOD}, as {OTHER_pronoun} would have wished it.
[give,doubt] If thou art there, {GOD}, take {OTHER_objective}, for {OTHER_pronoun} believed it.
[give,priest] By the old words we give {OTHER_nameDef} unto {GOD}, and the earth unto the earth.
[named] That was {GOD}'s doing, {SEASON}, I'd stake anything on it.
[named] Nobody can tell me {SEASON} just happened, that was {GOD}.
[named] {GOD} sent us {SEASON}, and we'd do well to remember it.
[named] My grandmother would have called it {GOD}'s season, and so do I.
[other] No, that was {GOD}, not {RIVAL}, and you know it.
[other] You've got it wrong, {SEASON} was {GOD}'s work, not {RIVAL}'s.
[other] {RIVAL}, really, when it was so plainly {GOD}?
[scoff] It was a hard season, that's all, and next year will be another.
[scoff] Weather is weather, nobody sent it.
[scoff] You'd blame a god for a draught under the door.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has not forgotten {SEASON}, and holds to it that it was {GOD}'s doing. Now the same season has come round again, and {A_pronoun} asks the council to keep a day against it: words said at {PLACE}, and the colony's people there to hear them, so that {GOD} remembers this house kindly.

The season has turned to where it was a year ago, when {SEASON} came down on the colony. {A_nameDef} says it was {GOD}, and that a day kept for {GOD} at {PLACE} would be a small price against another like it.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} has marked the day on the post by the door: a year since {SEASON} began. {GOD} sent it, {A_pronoun} says, and {GOD} should be asked at {PLACE}, with everyone there, not to send it twice.
[priest] It falls to the priest to remember such things. {A_nameDef} reminds the council of {SEASON}, which {A_pronoun} took for {GOD}'s, and asks for a day kept against its coming again.

li.label: Keep a day for {GOD} at {PLACE}
li.outcome: The council kept the day. {A_nameDef} led the words at {PLACE} that evening, and those who came stood with {A_objective} until it was done.

li.why: the council kept a day against {SEASON}

li.label: Let it pass
li.outcome: The council let the day pass. {A_nameDef} went to {PLACE} alone that evening and said the words there all the same.

plain.li: [tree] There, the tree is lit, now it feels like midwinter.
[tree] Lights on, and everyone come and look at it.
[treedark] It's switched on, but there's no power to light it.
[treedark] Somebody get the power running, or the tree stays dark.
[treelit] Still lit from last night, and it looks better every time.
[treelit] I just wanted a moment by the tree before supper.
[table] Gingerbread and the warm drinks are out by the table, help yourselves.
[table] It's all set out, and nobody touches it before supper.
[present] This one's for you, happy midwinter.
[present] I picked this one out for you, open it now.
[present] One each this year, and this is yours.
[snow] It's no snowman, it's a proper sculpture, come and see.
[snow] Snow's good for more than throwing, look at this.
